attrs.evidence: cas.mjs v0.2.0 (canonicalWire IS canonicalBytes, so the tree has ONE canonical encoder rather than two things called canonical that nothing compares; resolveArtifact requires the equality and names seven outcomes). jcs_vectors.mjs, gate `gov-nest`: 3/3 against published RFC 8785 data -- the RFC's own section 3.2.2/3.2.3 worked example, the reference suite's french.json, and a UTF-16 code-unit ordering vector in which U+1F602 (surrogate pair, first unit D83D) must precede U+FB33 and a code-point implementation puts it last. THREE VECTORS ARE NOT THE REFERENCE SUITE and full conformance is NOT claimed. Reproduced against the shipped P4 pack before repair: the same object indented resolved under one root (4880 vs 4509 bytes, resolveArtifact ok on both), and {"protocol":"TRVM-EVIL-v1", ... ,"protocol":"TRVM-NESTED-COMPOSITION-v1"} verified at ok:true with zero refusals.
attrs.statement: A CONTENT ADDRESS NAMES BYTES OR IT NAMES NOTHING. Hashing the PARSED object rather than the received octets makes a root a description of a parse result: any byte string that parses to that object resolves under it, so pretty and compact encodings share an address -- and a DUPLICATE OBJECT MEMBER NAME, which JSON.parse silently resolves in favour of the last occurrence, lets bytes saying one thing be AUTHENTICATED as an artifact saying another. That is a CROSS-IMPLEMENTATION hazard rather than a formatting preference: RFC 8259 calls parser behaviour on duplicate names unpredictable, I-JSON forbids them, RFC 8785 requires I-JSON, and an implementation keeping the FIRST duplicate would verify a different object under the same root while believing it had checked the same artifact. THE RULE: a resolver must require received_bytes === canonical_encoding(parsed_object) before it hashes anything, and the store must hold canonical bytes. Duplicate names, key reordering, alternate number spellings and whitespace are then all refused by ONE equality rather than by a special case each, and duplicate-key rejection is a CONSEQUENCE rather than a check -- canonical output emits every key once, so bytes containing a repeat can never equal the canonical form of what they parse to. THE ROOT IS TAKEN OVER THE PARSED OBJECT AND THE WIRE IS REQUIRED TO EQUAL IT, which is not the same as hashing the octets: what is authenticated and what is reasoned about must be one value. Human-readable encodings remain an export and presentation format. AND THE ENCODER MUST BE MEASURED AGAINST THE STANDARD RATHER THAN INSPECTED -- an encoder that sorted by CODE POINT instead of UTF-16 CODE UNIT passes every vector that contains no surrogate pair.
